stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}_i$, $i = 1, 2, 3$ be sites. Let
$u : \mathcal{C}_2 \to \mathcal{C}_1$ and
$v : \mathcal{C}_3 \to \mathcal{C}_2$ be continuous functors
which induce morphisms of sites. Then the functor
$u \circ v : \mathcal{C}_3 \to \mathcal{C}_1$ is continuous and
defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal{C}_1 \to \mathcal{C}_3$.
hypotheses:
Let $\mathcal{C}_i$, $i = 1, 2, 3$ be sites. Let
$u : \mathcal{C}_2 \to \mathcal{C}_1$ and
$v : \mathcal{C}_3 \to \mathcal{C}_2$ be continuous functors
which induce morphisms of sites.
conclusions:
the functor
$u \circ v : \mathcal{C}_3 \to \mathcal{C}_1$ is continuous and
defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal{C}_1 \to \mathcal{C}_3$.

reason: The composite of continuous functors is continuous and presheaf restriction satisfies (u∘v)^p=v^p∘u^p. Adjunction uniqueness identifies the inverse-image functor of the composite with the composition of both exact inverse-image functors, so the composite is a morphism of sites.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be sites. Let
$u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be continuous.
Assume furthermore the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the category $\mathcal{C}$ has a final object $X$ and
$u(X)$ is a final object of $\mathcal{D}$ , and
\item the category $\mathcal{C}$ has fibre products and
$u$ commutes with them.
\end{enumerate}
Then $u$ defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal{D} \to
\mathcal{C}$, in other words $u_s$ is exact.
hypotheses:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be sites. Let
$u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be continuous.
Assume furthermore the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the category $\mathcal{C}$ has a final object $X$ and
$u(X)$ is a final object of $\mathcal{D}$ , and
\item the category $\mathcal{C}$ has fibre products and
$u$ commutes with them.
\end{enumerate}
conclusions:
$u$ defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal{D} \to
\mathcal{C}$, in other words $u_s$ is exact.

reason: By the cited lemmas, continuous u preserving final objects and fibre products makes its induced sheaf pullback preserve finite limits. The proof explicitly invokes the directedness and morphism-of-indexing-category results needed to transfer exactness.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $f : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a morphism of sites given by the
functor $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$. Given any object $V$ of
$\mathcal{D}$ there exists a covering $\{V_j \to V\}$ such that for every
$j$ there exists a morphism $V_j \to u(U_j)$ for some object $U_j$
of $\mathcal{C}$.
hypotheses:
Let $f : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a morphism of sites given by the
functor $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$.
conclusions:
Given any object $V$ of
$\mathcal{D}$ there exists a covering $\{V_j \to V\}$ such that for every
$j$ there exists a morphism $V_j \to u(U_j)$ for some object $U_j$
of $\mathcal{C}$.

reason: Exact inverse image sends the final sheaf to the final sheaf. As this is the sheafification of u_p* and is locally nonempty, every V has a covering whose pieces yield actual objects of the comma category, hence maps V_j→u(U_j).
